events.title: Roman consuls take office on 1 January for the first time
events.description: Rome's consuls began their year of office on 1 January rather than in March, a change made to speed armies to the war in Hispania. The date became the start of the civil year and, eventually, of the modern new year.
events.html: Rome's consuls began their year of office on 1 January rather than in March, a change made to speed armies to the war in Hispania. The date became the start of the civil year and, eventually, of the modern new year.

events.title: Julius Caesar's Julian calendar comes into force
events.description: The solar calendar devised for Julius Caesar replaced Rome's erratic lunisolar reckoning. With a leap day every fourth year, it governed Europe for over sixteen centuries and underlies the Gregorian calendar used today.
events.html: The solar calendar devised for Julius Caesar replaced Rome's erratic lunisolar reckoning. With a leap day every fourth year, it governed Europe for over sixteen centuries and underlies the Gregorian calendar used today.

events.title: Roman Senate deifies the murdered Julius Caesar
events.description: Two years after his assassination, the Senate declared Julius Caesar a god of the Roman state as Divus Iulius. The honour let his adopted heir Octavian, the future Augustus, style himself 'son of a god'.
events.html: Two years after his assassination, the Senate declared Julius Caesar a god of the Roman state as Divus Iulius. The honour let his adopted heir Octavian, the future Augustus, style himself 'son of a god'.

events.title: Monk Telemachus killed trying to halt gladiatorial games in Rome
events.description: According to Theodoret, the monk Telemachus leapt into the arena to separate fighting gladiators and was stoned to death by the crowd. Emperor Honorius is said to have banned gladiatorial combat in response.
events.html: According to Theodoret, the monk Telemachus leapt into the arena to separate fighting gladiators and was stoned to death by the crowd. Emperor Honorius is said to have banned gladiatorial combat in response.

events.title: Stephen I crowned as the first King of Hungary
events.description: By traditional reckoning Grand Prince Stephen was crowned with a crown sent by Pope Sylvester II, making Hungary a Christian kingdom. Stephen's reign anchored the Magyars within Latin Christendom.
events.html: By traditional reckoning Grand Prince Stephen was crowned with a crown sent by Pope Sylvester II, making Hungary a Christian kingdom. Stephen's reign anchored the Magyars within Latin Christendom.

events.title: Portuguese navigators enter Guanabara Bay and name it Rio de Janeiro
events.description: Sailing along the Brazilian coast, a Portuguese expedition entered Guanabara Bay and, taking it for a river mouth, called it the 'River of January'. The city founded there in 1565 would become colonial Brazil's capital.
events.html: Sailing along the Brazilian coast, a Portuguese expedition entered Guanabara Bay and, taking it for a river mouth, called it the 'River of January'. The city founded there in 1565 would become colonial Brazil's capital.

events.title: Francis I becomes King of France on the death of Louis XII
events.description: Louis XII died without a son, and his twenty-year-old cousin and son-in-law Francis of Angoulême succeeded him. Francis became a great patron of the French Renaissance and a lifelong rival of Charles V.
events.html: Louis XII died without a son, and his twenty-year-old cousin and son-in-law Francis of Angoulême succeeded him. Francis became a great patron of the French Renaissance and a lifelong rival of Charles V.

events.title: Scotland begins its year on 1 January instead of 25 March
events.description: By decree of James VI, Scotland moved the start of its legal year from Lady Day to 1 January. England did not follow until 1752, so for 150 years the two kingdoms numbered their years differently.
events.html: By decree of James VI, Scotland moved the start of its legal year from Lady Day to 1 January. England did not follow until 1752, so for 150 years the two kingdoms numbered their years differently.

events.title: Charles II crowned King of Scots at Scone
events.description: Two years after his father's execution, Charles II was crowned at Scone by the Scottish Covenanters, the last coronation held there. His bid to regain England ended in defeat at Worcester that September.
events.html: Two years after his father's execution, Charles II was crowned at Scone by the Scottish Covenanters, the last coronation held there. His bid to regain England ended in defeat at Worcester that September.

events.title: Peter the Great's Russia adopts the Anno Domini year count
events.description: On Peter the Great's orders, Russia abandoned counting years from the Creation and began numbering them from the birth of Christ, starting the year on 1 January. It was an early step in his drive to Westernise Russia.
events.html: On Peter the Great's orders, Russia abandoned counting years from the Creation and began numbering them from the birth of Christ, starting the year on 1 January. It was an early step in his drive to Westernise Russia.

events.title: Jean-Baptiste Bouvet sights the world's most remote island
events.description: The French navigator Bouvet de Lozier sighted the ice-capped island that bears his name in the South Atlantic. Lying about 1,600 km from Antarctica, Bouvet Island is the most isolated island on Earth.
events.html: The French navigator Bouvet de Lozier sighted the ice-capped island that bears his name in the South Atlantic. Lying about 1,600 km from Antarctica, Bouvet Island is the most isolated island on Earth.

events.title: John Newton's 'Amazing Grace' is first used at Olney
events.description: The curate John Newton, a former slave-ship captain, introduced the hymn later known as 'Amazing Grace' at a New Year's Day service in Olney, Buckinghamshire. Newton later became an outspoken opponent of the slave trade.
events.html: The curate John Newton, a former slave-ship captain, introduced the hymn later known as 'Amazing Grace' at a New Year's Day service in Olney, Buckinghamshire. Newton later became an outspoken opponent of the slave trade.

events.title: Washington's army raises the Grand Union Flag at Prospect Hill
events.description: During the siege of Boston, the Continental Army hoisted the Grand Union Flag on Prospect Hill near Cambridge, Massachusetts. Combining thirteen stripes with the British Union, it served as the first flag of the united colonies.
events.html: During the siege of Boston, the Continental Army hoisted the Grand Union Flag on Prospect Hill near Cambridge, Massachusetts. Combining thirteen stripes with the British Union, it served as the first flag of the united colonies.

events.title: The Daily Universal Register becomes The Times
events.description: John Walter's three-year-old London paper published its first issue under the title The Times. It went on to become Britain's newspaper of record and one of the most influential journals in the world.
events.html: John Walter's three-year-old London paper published its first issue under the title The Times. It went on to become Britain's newspaper of record and one of the most influential journals in the world.

events.title: Act of Union creates the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
events.description: The union of Great Britain and Ireland took effect, abolishing the Irish Parliament and sending Irish members to Westminster. The arrangement lasted until the creation of the Irish Free State in 1922.
events.html: The union of Great Britain and Ireland took effect, abolishing the Irish Parliament and sending Irish members to Westminster. The arrangement lasted until the creation of the Irish Free State in 1922.

events.title: Giuseppe Piazzi discovers Ceres from Palermo
events.description: Searching the night sky from Palermo Observatory, Piazzi spotted a moving point of light: Ceres, the first object found in the asteroid belt. Long classed as a planet, then an asteroid, it is now termed a dwarf planet.
events.html: Searching the night sky from Palermo Observatory, Piazzi spotted a moving point of light: Ceres, the first object found in the asteroid belt. Long classed as a planet, then an asteroid, it is now termed a dwarf planet.

events.title: Haiti declares independence from France
events.description: Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed the independence of Haiti at Gonaïves after more than a decade of revolution. It became the first state founded by formerly enslaved people and the second independent nation in the Americas.
events.html: Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed the independence of Haiti at Gonaïves after more than a decade of revolution. It became the first state founded by formerly enslaved people and the second independent nation in the Americas.

events.title: United States bans the importation of enslaved Africans
events.description: The Act Prohibiting Importation of Slaves came into force, outlawing the transatlantic slave trade to the United States. Slavery itself and the domestic slave trade continued until the Civil War.
events.html: The Act Prohibiting Importation of Slaves came into force, outlawing the transatlantic slave trade to the United States. Slavery itself and the domestic slave trade continued until the Civil War.

events.title: Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein' is published anonymously
events.description: 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus' appeared in London in three volumes without its author's name. Mary Shelley's tale of a scientist and his creation is often called the first science-fiction novel.
events.html: 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus' appeared in London in three volumes without its author's name. Mary Shelley's tale of a scientist and his creation is often called the first science-fiction novel.

events.title: The Zollverein customs union takes effect in Germany
events.description: Led by Prussia, most German states abolished tariffs between them and formed a single customs area. The Zollverein bound their economies together and prepared the ground for political unification in 1871.
events.html: Led by Prussia, most German states abolished tariffs between them and formed a single customs area. The Zollverein bound their economies together and prepared the ground for political unification in 1871.

events.title: Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation comes into force
events.description: Abraham Lincoln's proclamation declared enslaved people in the rebelling Confederate states free. It turned the Civil War into a war against slavery and opened the Union army to Black soldiers.
events.html: Abraham Lincoln's proclamation declared enslaved people in the rebelling Confederate states free. It turned the Civil War into a war against slavery and opened the Union army to Black soldiers.

events.title: Queen Victoria proclaimed Empress of India at the Delhi Durbar
events.description: At a vast imperial assembly in Delhi, Viceroy Lord Lytton proclaimed Victoria Empress of India. The new title, devised by Disraeli, marked the British Raj's claim to succeed the Mughal emperors.
events.html: At a vast imperial assembly in Delhi, Viceroy Lord Lytton proclaimed Victoria Empress of India. The new title, devised by Disraeli, marked the British Raj's claim to succeed the Mughal emperors.

events.title: Italy proclaims the colony of Eritrea
events.description: Italy united its possessions on the Red Sea coast, centred on Massawa, into the colony of Eritrea. It became the base for Italian ambitions in the Horn of Africa, checked at Adwa in 1896.
events.html: Italy united its possessions on the Red Sea coast, centred on Massawa, into the colony of Eritrea. It became the base for Italian ambitions in the Horn of Africa, checked at Adwa in 1896.

events.title: Ellis Island opens as America's main immigration station
events.description: The federal immigration station on Ellis Island in New York Harbor processed its first arrivals, beginning with 17-year-old Annie Moore from Ireland. Some 12 million immigrants passed through it before 1954.
events.html: The federal immigration station on Ellis Island in New York Harbor processed its first arrivals, beginning with 17-year-old Annie Moore from Ireland. Some 12 million immigrants passed through it before 1954.

events.title: Six British colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia
events.description: New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania united under a federal constitution. Edmund Barton was sworn in as the first Prime Minister in Sydney's Centennial Park.
events.html: New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania united under a federal constitution. Edmund Barton was sworn in as the first Prime Minister in Sydney's Centennial Park.

events.title: Sun Yat-sen proclaims the Republic of China in Nanjing
events.description: Sun Yat-sen was sworn in as provisional president of the new Republic of China. Six weeks later the last Qing emperor abdicated, ending more than two thousand years of imperial rule.
events.html: Sun Yat-sen was sworn in as provisional president of the new Republic of China. Six weeks later the last Qing emperor abdicated, ending more than two thousand years of imperial rule.

events.title: World's first scheduled airline flight crosses Tampa Bay
events.description: The St Petersburg-Tampa Airboat Line flew its first paying passenger across Tampa Bay in a Benoist flying boat. The 23-minute hop launched scheduled commercial aviation, though the airline lasted only four months.
events.html: The St Petersburg-Tampa Airboat Line flew its first paying passenger across Tampa Bay in a Benoist flying boat. The 23-minute hop launched scheduled commercial aviation, though the airline lasted only four months.

events.title: Twenty-six Allied nations sign the Declaration by United Nations
events.description: Meeting in Washington, the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union, China and others pledged to fight the Axis together and make no separate peace. The term 'United Nations' later named the post-war organisation.
events.html: Meeting in Washington, the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union, China and others pledged to fight the Axis together and make no separate peace. The term 'United Nations' later named the post-war organisation.

events.title: American and British zones of Germany merge into the Bizone
events.description: The United States and Britain combined the economic administration of their occupation zones in Germany. The Bizone, joined by the French zone in 1949, became the nucleus of West Germany.
events.html: The United States and Britain combined the economic administration of their occupation zones in Germany. The Bizone, joined by the French zone in 1949, became the nucleus of West Germany.

events.title: Sudan becomes independent from Britain and Egypt
events.description: Sudan's parliament ended the Anglo-Egyptian condominium and the country became a sovereign republic. It was among the first African states to gain independence after the Second World War.
events.html: Sudan's parliament ended the Anglo-Egyptian condominium and the country became a sovereign republic. It was among the first African states to gain independence after the Second World War.

events.title: The European Economic Community comes into being
events.description: The Treaty of Rome took effect, creating a common market among France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. The EEC was the forerunner of today's European Union.
events.html: The Treaty of Rome took effect, creating a common market among France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. The EEC was the forerunner of today's European Union.

events.title: Batista flees Cuba as Castro's revolution triumphs
events.description: Dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Havana in the early hours, handing victory to Fidel Castro's guerrillas. The new revolutionary government later aligned with the Soviet Union, reshaping the Cold War in the Americas.
events.html: Dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Havana in the early hours, handing victory to Fidel Castro's guerrillas. The new revolutionary government later aligned with the Soviet Union, reshaping the Cold War in the Americas.

events.title: The Unix epoch: the zero point of computer time
events.description: Midnight UTC on this date was later chosen as the reference point from which Unix and its descendants count time in seconds. The convention still underpins timekeeping on most of the world's computers and phones.
events.html: Midnight UTC on this date was later chosen as the reference point from which Unix and its descendants count time in seconds. The convention still underpins timekeeping on most of the world's computers and phones.

events.title: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP, the birth of the modern internet
events.description: On this 'flag day' the US defence research network ARPANET required all hosts to use the TCP/IP protocols. The common standard allowed separate networks to interconnect, forming the internet.
events.html: On this 'flag day' the US defence research network ARPANET required all hosts to use the TCP/IP protocols. The common standard allowed separate networks to interconnect, forming the internet.

events.title: Brunei becomes fully independent from Britain
events.description: The oil-rich sultanate of Brunei ended nearly a century as a British protectorate and became a sovereign state under Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. It joined ASEAN within the week.
events.html: The oil-rich sultanate of Brunei ended nearly a century as a British protectorate and became a sovereign state under Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. It joined ASEAN within the week.

events.title: Montreal Protocol to protect the ozone layer enters into force
events.description: The treaty phasing out chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting chemicals came into effect. Ratified by every UN member, it is widely regarded as the most successful environmental agreement ever made.
events.html: The treaty phasing out chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting chemicals came into effect. Ratified by every UN member, it is widely regarded as the most successful environmental agreement ever made.

events.title: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully into two states
events.description: In the 'Velvet Divorce', Czechoslovakia dissolved by agreement into the Czech Republic and Slovakia. The separation was negotiated by politicians without a referendum and passed without violence.
events.html: In the 'Velvet Divorce', Czechoslovakia dissolved by agreement into the Czech Republic and Slovakia. The separation was negotiated by politicians without a referendum and passed without violence.

events.title: NAFTA takes effect between the United States, Canada and Mexico
events.description: The North American Free Trade Agreement came into force, phasing out most tariffs among the three countries and creating one of the world's largest free-trade areas. It was replaced by the USMCA in 2020.
events.html: The North American Free Trade Agreement came into force, phasing out most tariffs among the three countries and creating one of the world's largest free-trade areas. It was replaced by the USMCA in 2020.

events.title: The World Trade Organization is established
events.description: The WTO began work in Geneva, succeeding the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade of 1947. Unlike GATT, it covered services and intellectual property and had a binding system for settling trade disputes.
events.html: The WTO began work in Geneva, succeeding the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade of 1947. Unlike GATT, it covered services and intellectual property and had a binding system for settling trade disputes.

events.title: The euro is launched in eleven European countries
events.description: The euro became the official currency of eleven EU states, used at first for electronic transactions and financial markets. National notes and coins remained in circulation for three more years.
events.html: The euro became the official currency of eleven EU states, used at first for electronic transactions and financial markets. National notes and coins remained in circulation for three more years.

events.title: Euro notes and coins enter circulation
events.description: Euro banknotes and coins went into circulation in twelve countries, the largest currency changeover in history. Within two months the franc, mark, lira, peseta and other national currencies had ceased to be legal tender.
events.html: Euro banknotes and coins went into circulation in twelve countries, the largest currency changeover in history. Within two months the franc, mark, lira, peseta and other national currencies had ceased to be legal tender.

events.title: Bulgaria and Romania join the European Union
events.description: The two Balkan states became the European Union's 26th and 27th members. Their accession completed the EU's great eastward enlargement into the former communist bloc that began in 2004.
events.html: The two Balkan states became the European Union's 26th and 27th members. Their accession completed the EU's great eastward enlargement into the former communist bloc that began in 2004.

events.title: Powerful earthquake devastates Japan's Noto Peninsula
events.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck Ishikawa Prefecture on New Year's Day, triggering tsunami warnings, fires and landslides. Including later disaster-related deaths, more than 500 people lost their lives.
events.html: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck Ishikawa Prefecture on New Year's Day, triggering tsunami warnings, fires and landslides. Including later disaster-related deaths, more than 500 people lost their lives.

intl.name: New Year's Day
intl.description: Observed globally on the first day of the Gregorian calendar, New Year's Day marks the start of a new year and is one of the most widely celebrated public holidays in the world.
